questions.q: Per this lesson, why is a container-per-platform lab a more practical setup than installing Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL directly on your host operating system?
options: Each container is isolated and disposable — it can be stopped, deleted, and rebuilt from its image in minutes, unlike a bare-metal install
Containers make the databases run faster than a native install ever could
It's the only way to install more than one database engine on a single machine
Docker eliminates the need to ever configure a database engine
questions.explain: Bare-metal installs touch services, ports, and system configuration in ways that are hard to fully undo; a container is isolated and can simply be deleted and recreated.

questions.q: Where do the official MySQL and PostgreSQL Docker images come from, per this lesson?
options: Docker Hub, as official images (mysql and postgres) ready to pull directly
Oracle Container Registry, the same place as the Oracle image
They must be built manually from source before every use
A private registry that requires a paid subscription
questions.explain: MySQL and PostgreSQL both publish official images straight on Docker Hub, versioned by major release.

questions.q: Why does pulling the Oracle Database Free image require an extra step that MySQL and PostgreSQL don't?
options: Oracle's licensing model requires a free Oracle account and license acceptance through Oracle Container Registry, rather than a public Docker Hub pull
Oracle doesn't provide a container image at all
Oracle requires a paid enterprise license just to run a lab environment
Oracle images are only available on Windows, not Docker
questions.explain: Oracle's images are distributed through container-registry.oracle.com, gated by an account and a license click-through, unlike the public Docker Hub images for MySQL and PostgreSQL.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a named Docker volume in this lab setup, per this lesson?
options: It gives the container persistent storage so database files survive a container restart or rebuild
It speeds up network connections to the container
It automatically backs up the database to the cloud
It is required only for the Oracle container, not MySQL or PostgreSQL
questions.explain: A named volume attaches persistent storage to a container, so the underlying database files aren't lost when the container stops or is rebuilt.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where does the generic install/pull/run/verify setup flow get used again later in the course?
options: With platform-specific detail in Chapter 2 for Oracle, Chapter 7 for MySQL, and Chapter 12 for PostgreSQL
It is never used again — this lesson is a one-time exercise
Only in the course's final capstone project
Only for MySQL, since Oracle and PostgreSQL use a completely different process
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states this same flow — install, pull, run, verify — repeats with platform-specific variations in the installation lessons for each engine.
